This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/qingdao/ZSQD.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent cooling after mid-August heatwave conditions drives trader sentiment toward a modest maximum around 23–24°C on August 19.** Paris saw peaks near 37–38°C earlier in the month under strong high pressure and southerly warm-air advection, but forecasts now indicate weakening anticyclonic influence, increasing cloud cover, and light showers that limit daytime heating.

Official guidance and ensemble output (including European models) point to partly to mostly cloudy skies with a chance of sprinkles, reducing incoming solar radiation and enhancing evaporative cooling. This setup favors a daily high near the lower-to-mid 20s Celsius at Paris observing sites, consistent with the market’s tight clustering at 23°C (33%) and 24°C (28.5%).

The close split between these two outcomes reflects remaining model uncertainty in the precise timing and coverage of clouds or light rain, boundary-layer mixing, and subtle differences in 850 hPa temperatures or wind direction. A slightly earlier or thicker cloud deck, or marginally greater precipitation, would favor the lower end; clearer breaks or drier conditions would support the higher. Later outcomes above 25°C carry low probability given the established cooling trend and expected insolation deficit. Updated short-range model runs over the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalyst for any further market movement ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts for Shenzhen point to typical mid-August subtropical monsoon conditions, with high humidity, light winds, and scattered afternoon thunderstorms expected to moderate peak heating and keep the daily maximum near 32–34°C on August 19. Official outlooks from agencies such as the Shenzhen Meteorological Observatory and international models show a modest easing of the recent mid-month heat spell, supporting the market’s tight clustering around 32°C (30.5%) and 33°C (27.5%). Differentiating these outcomes hinges on small variations in cloud cover, convective timing, and any residual steering influence from distant tropical systems in the western Pacific, which can either enhance or suppress surface insolation and urban heat retention. Historical August climatology, with average highs near 32°C, reinforces why traders assign lower weight to 35°C or above while still leaving room for brief clearing that could nudge readings into the low 30s. Updated model runs and local observations over the next 48 hours will be key to resolving this narrow range.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ongoing southwest monsoon activity, with PAGASA forecasting 60% rain probability and a 24–31°C range for August 19 in Metro Manila, forms the core driver behind trader consensus favoring 28–29°C outcomes at combined 63.5% implied probability. Persistent cloud cover and convective showers from the monsoon reduce solar heating compared to drier conditions, keeping daily maxima near or slightly below the seasonal 30–31°C average. Differentiation among leading resolutions hinges on the precise timing, duration, and intensity of rainfall episodes, as heavier or more prolonged precipitation would suppress peaks toward 28°C while clearer intervals could allow 30°C. Short-term model updates from PAGASA and regional agencies over the next 48 hours will clarify steering patterns and moisture flux influencing these thresholds.
